title: Regional fallback cascade simulation and mitigation checklist
content:
Summary:
This is a working note for a tabletop + synthetic load simulation to reproduce a regional fallback cascade we saw in prod on 2025-09-28. The incident surface: repeated regional capacity shortages triggered progressive fallbacks to a secondary region, which in turn caused autoscaler thrash and noisy-tenant amplification on the second region leading to sustained throughput degradation across both regions.

Intent of this doc:
- Capture the incident hypothesis and the short remediation checklist for on-call responders.
- Outline a simulation plan to validate fallback and autoscaler behaviour under controlled synthetic load.
- Define a compact runbook checklist (playable on-call) and follow-ups to harden platform behaviour.

Observed signals during incident (high level):
- Spike in allocation failures: control plane returned 503s for allocation requests from hosted routing (metrics: allocator.alloc_fail_rate ↑ 250% over 10m).
- Autoscaler oscillation: scale-up -> sudden eviction -> scale-down loop in region-eu-2 (visible in autoscaler.events).
- Inter-region fallback traffic: routing logs show steady increase in routed requests to region-us-west as eu-2 drained.
- KV-cache amplification: cache miss rates in us-west increased for long-running chat sessions (cache.miss_rate ↑ 4x) leading to higher token CPU/GPU consumption per request.
- Latency tail rising: p99 went from 150ms to 700ms for generation endpoints.

Immediate on-call mitigation (what helped during the incident):
- Temporarily paused automated fallback policy (route policy -> set fallback.enabled=false) to stop further traffic concentration while we stabilized eu-2.
- Scoped burst capacity: allowed limited burst to region-us-west by increasing burst_quota for enterprise-tier customers only (reduced cross-tenant noise).
- Applied a short eviction policy tightening in eu-2 to prevent long-running low-priority workloads from taking fractional GPU slices during recovery.

Hypotheses we want to test in simulation:
1) Fallback concentration effect: routing fallback without rate shaping+priority causes arrival rate in target region to exceed autoscaler soft limits and triggers thrash.
2) Cache amplification loop: moving sessions across regions loses in-memory prefix/KV caching leading to higher per-token compute and triggers allocator pressure.
3) Autoscaler hysteresis gap: current autoscaler parameters (cooldown=60s, step=50%) are too aggressive for multi-region failover and cause oscillation.

Simulation plan (tabletop + synthetic):
- Environment: staging clusters corresponding to eu-2 and us-west (mirror config of prod autoscaler + allocator).
- Step 0: baseline capture – run steady load similar to normal 95th percentile for 30m and ingest traces/metrics.
- Step 1: induce controlled allocation failures in eu-2: simulate node drain events and kernel slowdowns to produce allocation 5xx for 2m.
- Step 2: enable production routing fallback rules and instrument per-route rate shaping (disabled in baseline) so we can flip it on/off.
- Step 3: replay traffic from a captured sample (10m window) but amplify by x2 for burst tests and x5 for worst-case.
- Step 4: vary autoscaler parameters across runs: cooldown {30s, 60s, 180s}, step {25%, 50%, 100%}, max-scale-rate {2x/min, 4x/min}.
- Step 5: measure outcomes – allocation fail rate, autoscaler event frequency, latency p95/p99, cache miss rate, GPU utilization distribution, eviction counts.

Success criteria for simulation:
- No autoscaler oscillation (<=1 scale event/min sustained over 10m) when fallback is active and arrival rate <= 3x baseline.
- Cache miss penalty quantified (expected extra GPU token load per session) and verified mitigation options can reduce it by >=50%.
- A routing rate-shaping policy (per-route backpressure) that keeps target-region queueing below 70% of autoscaler soft capacity.

On-call checklist (compact, 10 steps) — use when seeing cross-region fallback traffic spike:
1) Triage routing logs to confirm source region and target region(s) for fallback. Command: logs:route.client_fallback | filter region
2) Check allocator.alloc_fail_rate and allocator.queue_len for source region and target region.
3) If allocator.alloc_fail_rate > 10% and traffic redirected: temporarily pause global fallback via console (route policy -> fallback.enabled=false).
4) If target region shows autoscaler thrash (scale events > 3 in 10m): switch autoscaler to manual scale mode for a 10m window and set instance target to stable level (console/autoscaler.override=true).
5) Apply tenant priority gating: increase tenant isolation for unknown tenants (tenant.quota_policy -> reduce burst for non-enterprise).
6) Re-enable fallback with rate shaping: set per-route max-requests-per-second and smoothing window (recommendation: 30 rps smoothing per route, 10s window).
7) Monitor cache.miss_rate and if > 2x baseline, selectively route long-lived sessions back to original region where cache residency exists (sticky routing).
8) If eviction counts spike, reduce eviction aggressiveness to prevent cascading restarts (eviction.threshold -> +10% temporarily).
9) Communicate incident channel: post summary to #sre-ops and tag product and infra leads; include the temporary mitigations.
10) Open follow-up ticket (owner assigned) to run the simulation plan and collect artifacts for postmortem.

Quick runbook toggles (commands and locations):
- Toggle fallback: console -> routing -> fallback -> enabled (false/true) or api: POST /admin/routing/fallback {enabled:false}
- Autoscaler manual override: console -> autoscaler -> region -> override_target=N or api: POST /admin/autoscaler/override
- Tenant gating: console -> quotas -> tenant-policy or api: POST /admin/quotas/patch

Instrumentation additions (short-term):
- Add a fallback_rate metric (requests/sec caused by fallback) and expose per-route fallback_latency.
- Emit autoscaler.cooldown_remaining gauge so we can correlate decisions to sudden arrival spikes.
- Tag KV-cache misses with session_id and origin_region to measure cross-region penalty.

Follow-ups and owners (first pass):
- Ethan Clarke: run the synthetic simulation and capture metrics and traces (due 2025-10-22).
- Marta Ruiz: prototype per-route rate-shaping middleware and add a simple backoff policy to the router (due 2025-11-05).
- Jordan Lee: audit current autoscaler defaults and propose safer defaults for multi-region failover (due 2025-10-30).
- Priya Menon (author): draft the post-incident runbook update with the compact checklist and test results (due 2025-11-08).

Open questions / risks to discuss during tabletop:
- How do we balance customer SLA obligations when we gate fallback? (trade-off: localized degradation vs global cascade)
- Do we prefer sticky routing for long-lived sessions at the cost of slightly higher latency for newcomers?
- Is burst quota per-tenant the right lever versus global per-route shaping?

Notes to self:
- Keep simulation runs reproducible: snapshot autoscaler state and routing rules before each run.
- Record pcap of inter-region routing control messages during runs to inspect any race in route updates.
- If we confirm cache amplification is the main culprit, prioritize adding cross-region KV warm-start for pinned sessions.

Appendix (quick artifacts):
- Short timeline of the prod incident (high level): 2025-09-28 14:02 – allocation errors start in eu-2; 14:07 – routing fallback starts; 14:12 – us-west autoscaler thrash begins; 14:40 – mitigations applied (fallback paused + burst gating); 15:05 – partial recovery.
- Key dashboards to watch: infra/allocations, autoscaler/events, routing/fallback-rate, kvcache/miss_rate, endpoint/latency-p99.

If anything in this doc needs to be formalized into the canonical runbook, mark it with [MAKE-OFFICIAL]. For now this is a working log for simulation design and an on-call compact checklist.
